rules.statement: Make sure only one workflow publishes packages to nuget.org for a given release event; when you add a new publish workflow, remove or retire the old one.
rules.why: Two publish paths on the same release make the second one fail on a version that already exists, so every release shows a failing run. An unused long-lived API key also stays in use.
rules.check: In a workflow diff that adds or changes a `release: published` (or similar) trigger that pushes to nuget.org, look for any other workflow in the repository that also pushes packages on the same event.

rules.statement: Make sure every documentation link to a file anchor points at a heading that exists in the target file, and that the target actually holds the content the link promises.
rules.why: A dead anchor drops readers at the top of the target file, where they can't find the content they were promised.
rules.check: For each added or changed Markdown link of the form `file.md#anchor`, confirm the target file has a matching heading and holds the described content.

rules.statement: Don't ask for changes to files the project template owns, such as `.claude/commands/` or `build/ProjectTemplate.props`, in a downstream repository; send the problem upstream to NCodeGroup/project-template instead.
rules.why: Every template update replaces template-owned files, so a local edit gets overwritten. These choices belong to the template.
rules.check: Before reporting a gap or defect in a file, find out whether the project template supplies and replaces that file. If it does, report it as an upstream template issue rather than asking for a local fix.

rules.statement: When a build change makes a library's AssemblyVersion lower than the one its last release shipped with (for example, pinning it to Major.0.0.0 after releases shipped the full version), flag it as a binary break and require either an explicit `<AssemblyVersion>` in the repository's own props or a note in CHANGELOG.md.
rules.why: Consumers compiled against the higher assembly version can fail with FileLoadException when only the new assembly is deployed, so a minor or patch release becomes a breaking change.
rules.check: In a diff to versioning properties in props or csproj files, compare the resulting AssemblyVersion with the version the last release shipped, and look for an explicit override or a CHANGELOG entry.

rules.statement: Don't report the template's Dependabot auto-merge workflow, which auto-merges only a pull request whose one change is the NCode Review pin, as breaking the no-auto-merge rule when the repository's AGENTS.md records that it accepts the ADR-0006 exception.
rules.why: The template's ADR-0006 documents this narrow exception, and the repository has recorded that it accepts it.
rules.check: Before flagging `gh pr merge --auto` in the code-review auto-merge workflow, look in AGENTS.md conventions for a recorded acceptance of the ADR-0006 exception, and confirm the workflow limits auto-merge to NCode Review pin bumps.

rules.statement: Don't report a project's Landing `draft: no` setting as breaking the agents-open-drafts rule when the diff doesn't change it: ADR-0006 allows pull requests to be ready by default, and the setting is the project's choice.
rules.why: The value is the project's existing Landing choice, which ADR-0006 permits. A template update that leaves it unchanged has nothing to fix.
rules.check: Before flagging `draft: no` in AGENTS.md Landing settings, check whether the diff actually changes the value. If it doesn't, don't report it.
